mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during FEDFUNDS > 2.0 regimes.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which precedes a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE < previous month
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, returns are negative despite the labor signal, with IC < -0.1 and p-value > 0.05 in a two-sample test.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105 suggests weakening supply-side demand, which predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: INDPRO recovers without a corresponding SPX return reversal over the 20-day window.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5% for two consecutive months, it indicates persistent demand pressure, which is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: No significant positive return in the 20-day window despite CPIAUCSL > 2.5 for two months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 4-week decline in residential housing starts (HOUST) is interpreted as a housing soft landing, which triggers a positive S&P 5-day forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain negative despite the housing signal (IC < -0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in retail activity proxy RSAFS below 500,000 suggests softening demand, which is associated with a negative S&P 20-day forward return.

failure_condition: No negative return observed when RSAFS declines (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) without a corresponding drop in UNRATE indicates labor market stress, predicting a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE unchanged
failure_condition: Return is positive despite the labor signal (IC < -0.1, p < 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in UNRATE below 4% combined with FEDFUNDS above 1.5% suggests a balance sheet tightening, which precedes a positive S&P 60-day forward return in expansionary regimes.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0 AND FEDFUNDS > 1.5 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the trigger regime.
